headline: Enron: a pipeline giant that wants to trade gas
text: Enron, the Houston company formed in 1985 by the merger of Houston Natural Gas and InterNorth, owns one of the largest natural gas pipeline networks in the United States, more than 36,000 miles of pipe. Chairman Kenneth Lay is adding power plants and has started a 'Gas Bank' that lets producers and buyers lock in gas supplies and prices years ahead. The company is still living down 1987, when traders at its oil-trading unit in Valhalla, New York, ran up losses that Enron put at $85 million.
imageCaption: Enron's headquarters complex in downtown Houston, Texas

headline: LDDS: cheap long distance from Mississippi
text: LDDS, a long-distance telephone company from Jackson, Mississippi, resells calls over AT&T's network at a discount to small businesses. Founded in 1983 in a Hattiesburg coffee shop and run since 1985 by Bernard Ebbers, a former basketball coach and motel owner, it grows by buying small regional rivals and paying with its own shares; in 1989 it merged with Advantage Companies.
imageCaption: Downtown Hattiesburg, Mississippi, where LDDS was founded in 1983

headline: McDonald's opens in Moscow
text: The first McDonald's in the Soviet Union opened on Moscow's Pushkin Square on 31 January, after 14 years of negotiations led by McDonald's Canada's president George Cohon. About 38,000 customers queued for hours on the first day, a company record.
imageCaption: Plaque at the McDonald's on Pushkin Square, Moscow: 'Roubles only restaurant'

headline: Cisco Systems goes public
text: Cisco Systems, a Menlo Park maker of routers that link different computer networks, sold 2.8 million shares to the public on February 16 at $18 each. The shares closed the first day at $22.25. The company, founded in 1984 by two Stanford computer staff, had sales of about $28 million in its last fiscal year and is profitable; the offering values it at roughly $224 million.
source: https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/business-and-management/cisco-systems-goes-public (read 2026-10-03); market value at IPO from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cisco (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Cisco's AGS router, the multiprotocol router Cisco was selling when it went public

headline: Coca-Cola's best year: 76% return in 1989, a split and a bigger dividend
text: Coca-Cola's net income per share rose 73% in 1989 to 4.92 dollars, helped by the Columbia gain, and the total return to shareholders was 76%. The board raised the dividend 18%, the largest increase since 1960, and recommends a two-for-one stock split. Over the 1980s the share price rose almost sevenfold and the market value grew from 4.3 to 26 billion dollars.

headline: Tokyo shares crash as the yen falls
text: The Bank of Japan raised its discount rate by a full point to 5.25% on 20 March to stop the yen's fall and the slide in shares. On 22 March the dollar reached a three-year high of 155 yen and the Nikkei fell below 29,000 for the first time since November 1988; it ended the month just under 30,000, down about a quarter from its December record. On 27 March the Finance Ministry told banks to limit their lending for property.
source: https://www.upi.com/Archives/1990/03/20/Bank-of-Japan-increases-discount-rate-1-percent/5094637909200/ (via search, 2026-10-03); https://www.upi.com/Archives/1990/03/21/Dollar-soars-Tokyo-stocks-nosedive/7995637995600/ (via search, 2026-10-03); https://www.upi.com/Archives/1990/03/30/Stocks-plunge-337-in-Tokyo/9971638773200/ (via search, 2026-10-03); https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/バブル崩壊 (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The trading floor of the Tokyo Stock Exchange

headline: Windows 3.0 gives PCs what made the Mac special
text: Microsoft launched Windows 3.0 on 22 May. It gives ordinary IBM-compatible PCs a screen with windows, icons and a mouse much like the Macintosh, at lower prices. Apple's Macs still sell well, but the PCs are catching up.
imageCredit: OS by Microsoft Corporation/Screenshot by PantheraLeo1359531

headline: Iraq's invasion of Kuwait sends shares down 9 percent
text: Iraq invaded Kuwait on 2 August; oil prices jumped and markets around the world fell. The rise in energy prices pushed long-term interest rates up, and share prices, which had set records in July, fell substantially. The S&P 500 lost 9% in August to 322.56.
imageCaption: American troops sent to Saudi Arabia after Iraq's invasion of Kuwait; President Bush addresses them at an air base

headline: The Gulf crisis ends the reunification boom
text: Since Iraq invaded Kuwait on 2 August, oil prices have jumped and stock markets have been falling worldwide. After the boom in German shares that followed the opening of the Berlin Wall, investors are now selling. BMW lost more than a fifth of its value in September.
source: Die Zeit, 'Aktien haben ihren Reiz verloren', 17 August 1990, https://www.zeit.de/1990/34/aktien-haben-ihren-reiz-verloren (read 2026-10-03); Die Zeit, 'Markt-Report: Verkaufsdruck aus London', 31 August 1990, https://www.zeit.de/1990/36/verkaufsdruck-aus-london (read 2026-10-03); data/out/bmw.json (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: US F-15E fighter aircraft parked in Saudi Arabia during Operation Desert Shield, autumn 1990

headline: Tokyo's crash drags Sony down
text: Japanese share prices have collapsed this year: by 30 August the market had fallen to half its December 1989 record, as the Bank of Japan raised its discount rate step by step to 6%. Sony shares fell 22% in dollars in September.
imageCaption: The market centre of the Tokyo Stock Exchange

headline: Germany is one country again
text: At midnight on 3 October the German Democratic Republic joined the Federal Republic and Germany was reunited, eleven months after the Wall opened. The Two Plus Four treaty, signed in Moscow on 12 September by the two German states and the four wartime Allies, restores Germany's full sovereignty. On 20 September both German parliaments approved the unification treaty by large majorities.
imageCaption: State ceremony for German unity, Berlin, 3 October 1990

headline: Cisco breaks out as the market recovers
text: After a fall of about 22% between mid-July and October 11, the stock market started to recover in the second half of October. Cisco's shares were among the first to break out to new highs. The company has reported nine straight quarters of large earnings increases, its earnings have grown about 257% a year for three years, and analysts expect another 145% rise in 1991.
imageCaption: An early Cisco AGS router, 1986 model

headline: Apple goes cheap: the Macintosh Classic for 999 dollars
text: On 15 October Apple presented the Macintosh Classic and the Macintosh LC, its first Macs priced for schools and homes: chairman John Sculley said prices would start at 1,000 dollars, less than half of what a Mac used to cost. Apple wants the Macintosh in many more hands. Investors are uneasy, because cheaper machines earn thinner profits on each sale.

headline: 1990 in review: recession and the Gulf crisis cost 7 percent
text: The S&P 500 fell 7% in 1990 to 330.22; the Dow, down 18% from July to its low of 2,381.99 on 16 October, ended at 2,633.66, off 4.3%. Economists say the economy is in recession, and how deep it gets depends on war or peace in the Gulf. Banks are hurting from bad property loans: Citicorp, the biggest, plans to cut its dividend and 8,000 jobs, and the Fed cut its discount rate to 6.5 percent in December.
imageCaption: President Bush has Thanksgiving dinner with US troops in Saudi Arabia, 22 November 1990

headline: Philip Morris adds Jacobs Suchard to its food empire
text: This year Philip Morris bought Jacobs Suchard, the Swiss coffee and chocolate maker, for 4.1 billion dollars, and combined General Foods and Kraft into Kraft General Foods, the world's second-largest food company. Food now brings in more than half of the group's revenue, but cigarettes still earn most of the profit.
source: https://www.referenceforbusiness.com/history2/72/Philip-Morris-Companies-Inc.html (read 2026-10-03; the month of the Jacobs Suchard purchase is not given there); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Foods (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Toblerone, one of the Jacobs Suchard chocolate brands

headline: Wal-Mart reaches California and the billion-dollar profit
text: Wal-Mart opened its first stores in California this year and now trades from coast to coast. Its US sales have roughly quadrupled since 1985 to about 32 billion dollars. In 1989 it became the first retailer to earn more than one billion dollars after tax in a year, with 1,402 stores and 272,000 employees.
